object_description: terraced and staggered one-to-three-story school structure
design_condition: The structure follows the gently sloping topography, stays close to the existing building, and extends the ensemble through related outdoor rooms, alleys, arcades, and preserved play areas.

positive.statement: The differentiated scale and compositional balance establish a convincing connection to the existing complex and park.

position.rationale: Broad marker spans the stepped masses that mediate between existing complex and park.

positive.statement: The open-air school concept creates a wide range of teaching possibilities and gives the place a characteristic identity.

position.rationale: Placed across the terraced building and its repeated open edge conditions.

positive.statement: The concise building structure provides high practical value in the transition from outside to inside.

position.rationale: Visible stepped perimeter and veranda-like edges identify an exterior-interior transition zone.

positive.statement: The free-standing pavilion offers great benefit to the district as a continuation of the ensemble.

position.rationale: Detached upper-right pavilion is clearly separated from the main staggered structure.

positive.statement: Space, structure, light, rhythm, and proportion grow together in a joyful interplay.

position.target: space, structure, light, rhythm, and proportion
position.rationale: Broad marker covers the repeated terraced massing and vertically varied elevations.

positive.statement: The partial basement appropriately responds to the unfavorable subsoil and high groundwater level.

position.rationale: Lower southern portion is assigned as the likely partly sunken level.

positive.statement: The interaction of classrooms, open-air rooms, and covered zones provides varied learning and work spaces.

position.target: classrooms, open-air rooms, and covered zones
position.rationale: Placed along the stepped middle zone where solid and open bands alternate.

positive.statement: The day school can be ideally divided into zones for younger and older children.

position.rationale: Distributed toward one end of the elongated ensemble as a plausible age-group division.

positive.statement: The use of wood in the construction and the green roof enables achievement of the ECO standard.

position.rationale: Roof marker follows the distinct upper-right mass visible in the top and elevation views.

negative.statement: The fragmentary model negates the true dimensions of the expansive open volumes and raises doubts about scale and urban planning classification.

position.target: fragmentary model and expansive open volumes
position.rationale: Broad marker covers the fragmented terraced composition and its large intervening gaps.

negative.statement: The generous spatial offer sometimes comes at the expense of rooms that are too small.

position.rationale: Estimated within a smaller stepped wing rather than the broad central volume.

negative.statement: The close interconnection of the spatial offerings leads to a somewhat confusing access situation.

position.rationale: Central interconnection of staggered wings is the most plausible access conflict zone.

negative.statement: The location of the day school somewhat limits the overview of the area.

position.rationale: Assigned to the peripheral upper-right zone where oversight of the broader site is limited.

negative.statement: Balconies and terraces reduce daylight and limit passive solar use in winter.

position.rationale: Upper stepped edges indicate the likely balcony and terrace zones affecting facade exposure.

negative.statement: A consistent installation and building technology concept is not apparent, and access is not guaranteed throughout.

position.rationale: Building-wide systems are estimated through the central mass because no components are distinguishable.

negative.statement: The effort required to achieve the energy standard across the project is great.

position.rationale: Energy-standard effort and cost are non-spatial judgments.

negative.statement: The large external floor areas result in comparatively high construction and maintenance costs.

position.rationale: Placed across the lower exterior bands surrounding the fragmented building.
